subject: geography
title: Latitude and longitude
objective: Use coordinates to locate places on Earth.

lesson.opening: Every place on Earth can be located by two coordinates: how far north or south, and how far east or west.

sections.heading: Parallels of latitude
sections.body: Lines of latitude run east–west and measure distance north or south of the equator, from 0° at the equator to 90° at the poles. Because they are parallel, a degree of latitude covers roughly the same distance everywhere, about 111 km.

sections.heading: Meridians of longitude
sections.body: Lines of longitude run north–south between the poles and measure distance east or west of the prime meridian at 0°. They converge at the poles, so a degree of longitude covers less ground the farther you are from the equator.

sections.heading: Writing a coordinate
sections.body: Latitude is given first, then longitude — for example 30°N, 90°W. The equator and the prime meridian divide the globe into hemispheres.

activities.prompt: Which lines run east–west and measure distance north or south of the equator?
Lines of longitude all meet at…
A place at 30°N, 90°W is closest to…
Why does one degree of longitude cover less ground near the poles?
Explain why latitude alone cannot locate a place.
activities.instructions: Two or three sentences are enough.
activities.context: Latitude gives only north–south position. Many places share the same latitude, so a second coordinate is needed.
rubric: explains that longitude is also needed
